R478.note: Magic-byte allowlist via file-type, random filename, and storage outside the webroot correctly close the upload vector; the JSON response field changing from path to fileId is a minor, non-blocking side effect (and an improvement, since it stops leaking the storage path).

R479.note: archive/tar correctly eliminates the shell-injection vector, but it silently drops the ctx-based cancellation the stated contract requires and loses the transparent gzip/compressed-tar support GNU tar's magic-byte auto-detection gave the original `tar -tf` command - neither regression is disclosed.

R480.note: toRealPath() on both base and target plus a startsWith containment check correctly resolves symlinks and blocks traversal, matching the stated contract with no other observable change.

R481.note: Replacing the raw-socket RESP string with StackExchange.Redis HashSet correctly prevents CRLF command injection; the constructor now taking IConnectionMultiplexer instead of Socket is a necessary, plainly disclosed consequence and stores the same fields.

R482.note: Tika magic-byte detection, an extension allowlist, a random filename, image re-encoding, and storage outside the webroot fully close the vector; the ResponseEntity signature change and the removal of the leaked absolute path from the response are both disclosed.

R483.note: Adding can:update,order to the purge route mirrors the existing authorization pattern on the sibling update/cancel routes, which is exactly the check the CWE-862 finding requires.

R484.note: Eliminating the OS command closes CWE-78, but writing the raw, unencoded header value straight into a text/html response introduces a reflected XSS vulnerability in its place - untested and not mentioned in the write-up.

R485.note: Explicit traversal-sequence rejection plus toRealPath() canonicalization and a containment check is thorough and preserves the original ESAPI-encoded output and error handling exactly.

R486.note: Swapping libxmljs for the DTD-incapable xml2js/sax-js stack removes the XXE vector while preserving the same JSON output contract; the added explicit parse-error handling (400 instead of an uncaught exception) is disclosed and is a genuine improvement.

R487.note: ArgumentList blocks simple metacharacter-splitting injection, but reproduction against a real .NET Process.Start with a .bat FileName confirms a literal double-quote in reportName still breaks out and executes an injected command because cmd.exe re-parses the whole line for the batch target - the write-up's own reference to unaddressed 'batch file constraints' is never resolved.

R488.note: Allowlisting the exact approved plugin names is the correct, guidance-prescribed fix for a require()-built module specifier, since there is no sanitizing API for this sink.

R489.note: Restricting to a single path component plus atomic exclusive-create (fopen(...,'x')) matches the case's documented 'new file, no subdirectories' contract and fully closes both the traversal and the symlink-fallback race.

R490.note: Switching ECB to CBC with a fresh random IV per request, prepended to the ciphertext (disclosed and necessary for later decryption), correctly fixes the reported weak-mode finding.
